A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CryoBoltz, with the same authors, guidance framework, and retained experiments despite the revised title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original structure-prediction experiments on synthetic STP10 and CH67 maps and experimental P-glycoprotein maps, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds evaluations on Pma1, CYP102A1, and YbbAP, together with MSA-subsampling comparisons and experimental-map ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains pretrained Boltz-1, DPS-based guidance, weighted-k-means point clouds, Sinkhorn global guidance, density-based local guidance, and unguided warm-up and relaxation. V2 adjusts experimental scheduling and map preprocessing without introducing a different model, guidance objective, or core method component.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from three biomolecular systems to six. Alongside the retained synthetic datasets and four P-glycoprotein states, v2 evaluates active/inhibited Pma1, open/closed CYP102A1, and bound/unbound YbbAP. This substantially broadens experimental validation to additional protein systems and map conditions, including a 6.5 Å map.

E2.justification: V2 adds Boltz-1 with random MSA subsampling as an evaluated comparator in Table 1 and new Table B1; v1 only discussed MSA-based alternatives. This introduces direct comparison with an important strategy for generating conformational diversity across the evaluated systems. Unguided Boltz-1, AlphaFold3, and ModelAngelo remain.

E3.justification: The reported real-map schedule changes from 125/25/25/25 warm-up/global/local/relaxation steps to 100/50/25/25, retaining 200 total steps; synthetic settings remain unchanged. Added experiments specify five samples at each MSA depth of 64–1024 and dataset-specific map preprocessing. ModelAngelo additionally receives TM-score evaluation. The existing best-of-25 selection framework is retained.

E4.justification: V1 ablates global and local guidance only on synthetic maps. V2 adds these ablations for all ten experimental maps in Table B1, testing whether their combination remains beneficial under real measurement conditions and revealing exceptions. Appendix sample-quality distributions also expand to the six newly evaluated experimental states.

E5.justification: Both versions use three replicates with 25 samples per replicate and report means with 95% confidence intervals for samples selected by map fit. V1 Table B1 becomes v2 Table B2 with the same uncertainty-reporting practice. Additional rows and changed interval values do not establish a new statistical procedure or increased replication.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for the new systems, MSA baseline, and experimental-map ablations. For example, Table 2 reports Pma1 inhibited-state all-atom RMSD of 1.999 Å for CryoBoltz versus 6.140 Å for Boltz-1. Retained results also change: STP10 inward CryoBoltz Cα RMSD changes from 0.379 to 0.371 Å, and P-glycoprotein scores are revised. The latter accompany a changed guidance schedule, so they are not same-setting performance gains. Aggregate mean rows are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the forward-model assumptions, and Appendix A.4's optimal-transport and Sinkhorn definitions retain their mathematical substance. Using a variable phase length in the cosine schedule expresses the experimental scheduling adjustment rather than a new theoretical result. Neither version adds proofs or theorems.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains inference-time cryo-EM guidance that improves conformational coverage without retraining. However, v2 narrows the consistency claim: v1 says guidance ensures consistency with observations 'by construction,' whereas v2's Discussion says it biases sampling toward consistent models. The expanded experiments support the retained contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: V2 newly identifies principled validation of models derived from low-resolution maps as unresolved. Section 4.1 also makes applicability restrictions explicit through selection of systems with at most two unique chains and fewer than 2,200 residues. The ablation interpretation becomes qualified to 'most' experimental maps. Existing optimization-instability and initialization limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address absent from v1. Appendix A documents preprocessing for the added systems, including density thresholds, ten-voxel padding, and YbbAP component removal at size threshold 100, alongside dataset-dependent guidance schedules. Existing software, alignment, and A100 hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for deposited structures and the YbbAP study while retaining the methodological literature. Section 3.4 replaces the criticism of ROCKET's architectural restriction with a contrast emphasizing CryoBoltz's atomic-space optimization, and removes the description of ADP-3D as the 'first and only' demonstration. These are limited positioning refinements.

P1.justification: The title changes from guidance of 'AlphaFold3' to 'protein structure prediction.' V2 polishes prose, groups results into synthetic and experimental dataset subsections, and adds a short conclusion. The introduction, background, method exposition, and appendix organization remain substantially recognizable; added experiments do not constitute wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially expanded and reorganized: Tables 1 and 2 gain comparator or system columns and rows, Figure 6 and experimental-ablation Table B1 are added, and the original Table B1 becomes an expanded Table B2. The original RMSD histogram figure is split into synthetic and experimental figures with additional panels. Figure 2 replaces numerical stage boundaries with symbolic phase lengths.

improvement.justification: V1's real-data evidence depended on one protein system and lacked a tested MSA-diversification comparator. V2 substantially strengthens that evidence through three additional experimental systems, direct MSA-subsampling comparisons, and real-map guidance ablations that expose both benefits and exceptions. Clearer applicability limits, a more measured consistency claim, and added reproducibility information further improve the paper. Selection still favors systems with usable initial predictions, but the broader validation meaningfully strengthens the conclusions within that scope.
